messages:
jordan_acme: Hey support, heads up. Our search re-ranker started returning values >1 and ordering that doesn't match our offline dot-product checks. We feed embeddings from your embedding endpoint into /v1/rerank. Samples attached.

maya.patel: Thanks. Can you paste one exact request/response (sanitized) and the model names used for embedding and rerank?

jordan_acme: Sure. Workflow: generate embeddings at ingest with model embed-large-1536, persist as base64 in Postgres. Later, calls to /v1/rerank use model rerank-standard-1024. Example payloads below.

```
POST /v1/embeddings
{"model":"embed-large-1536","input":"Customer text"}
# resp: {"embedding":[0.002, -0.11, ..., 0.003]}  // length 1536

POST /v1/rerank
{"model":"rerank-standard-1024","query_embedding":[<1536 floats>],"candidate_embeddings":[[...],[...]]}
# resp: {"scores":[1.45, 0.12, -0.22]}
```

maya.patel: That looks like a dimension mismatch. Our rerank models expect 1024 dims; you sent 1536. Does your client ever re-embed with a 1024 model?

jordan_acme: We switched embedding models last quarter and didn't reprocess historical docs. We assumed the rerank endpoint would internally normalize/pad. Our local dot-prod between 1024-sliced vectors and full 1536 dims is consistent in ordering, but the server output isn't.

eng-ml-simone: Investigating. Current rerank path does not enforce strict dimension equality. It forwards vectors into a kernel selector that attempts to find a compatible kernel; if dims differ it may choose a fallback that pads or slices buffers depending on hardware layout. We do L2-normalize before scoring which explains non-0..1 numbers and sign flips. This is unsafe.

sre-anna: We saw a similar symptom in pre-prod where a mixed-dim traffic spike produced anomalous positive-heavy scores. The old fallback kernel used 32-byte alignment padding; combined with normalization that produced inflated dot products. We added a staging guard but it never rolled.

alex.kim: Immediate next steps for support: provide a clear workaround and offer re-embedding assistance. For engineering: block mismatched dims at the API surface and schedule a hotfix.

maya.patel: Draft support reply: "Thanks — your saved embeddings are 1536-dimensional (embed-large-1536) but your rerank model expects 1024. Options: 1) Recompute embeddings using a 1024-d embedding model; 2) Re-run rerank calls using embeddings from a compatible embedding model; 3) We can re-embed your index as a one-off (we can estimate cost). We're patching the service to return 400 with a clear error when dims mismatch." Thoughts?

jordan_acme: That works. Prefer server-side validation so we don't have silent incorrect scores. Also can you share a quick SQL snippet to check dims for our persisted embeddings?

maya.patel: SQL for JSON array embeddings: `SELECT json_array_length(embedding::json) as dim FROM documents WHERE id = 'xxx';`

If base64 float32 blob: `python` snippet: `b = base64.b64decode(emb); dim = len(b)//4`

eng-runtime-tom: For the hotfix I'll add strict validation in the rerank ingress: if len(query_embedding) != model_spec.dim OR any(len(c) != model_spec.dim for c in candidates) -> return 400 {"error":"embedding dimension mismatch: expected 1024 got 1536"}. We'll also instrument a counter `rerank.dim_mismatch` tagged by model and customer.

eng-ml-simone: In addition: add a migration check job to scan object storage/DB for vectors with dims that don't match the expected family and surface a CSV of affected customer IDs. We'll include an opt-in one-off reembed service in support playbook. PR will include unit tests and a canary rollout plan.

sre-anna: Deployment signal plan: canary 5% -> 20% -> 100% with 15m windows and synthetic probe after each step. Probe will POST a deliberately mismatched payload and expect 400. Also monitor `5xx` and latency P95.

alex.kim: Assign SR and notify billing: if customer re-embeds many docs we may need to credit them — flag for finance.

support-bot: SR created: SR-2974 (rerank-dim-mismatch). Owner: eng-ml-simone. SLA: 48h.

eng-ml-simone: PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-service/pull/870 (adds validation, tests, telemetry). I'll request eng-runtime and eng-sre reviews.

maya.patel: Sent customer reply with workaround + SQL examples and offered re-embed help. Customer responded: "Thanks, we'll hold reprocessing for now and wait for fix."

jordan_acme: Quick follow-up Q: will the `embedding_model` parameter on rerank let you pick the proper rerank kernel automatically if we can't re-embed?

eng-runtime-tom: Not today. `embedding_model` was planned for latter-quarter but not yet shipped. Short-term we should accept it as advisory and map model families to kernels, but still validate dims.

eng-ml-simone: Action items captured in PR and SR: 1) server validation + tests 2) telemetry query to find past mismatches (last 90d) 3) support reembed offer 4) optional migration reembed job for customers 5) consider `embedding_model` advisory support. I'll run telemetry in staging and paste results in SR.

sre-anna: Post-deploy: run retrospective log query: `grep -R "accepted .*-dim vector" /var/log/rerank | cut -d' ' -f3 | sort | uniq -c` and map to account ids. We'll message customers in the sweep.

alex.kim: Thanks all. Priority P2. Keep SR updated. jordan_acme: we'll ping when hotfix is live and can assist with re-embedding if you choose.

jordan_acme: Appreciate it. Will test again once fix is in canary.

-- end of thread --
